meaning:
ἐξ-άγω
[in LXX chiefly for יָצָא hi. ;]
to lead out: with accusative, Mrk.15:20, Jhn.10:3, Act.5:19 7:36 16:37-39; before ἔξω, Luk.24:50; ἐκ, Act.7:40 12:17 13:17, Heb.8:9; εἰς, Act.21:38.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: When they had mocked him, they took the purple off him, and put his own garments on him. They led him out to crucify him.
He led them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands, and blessed them.
The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name, and leads them out.
But an angel of the Lord opened the prison doors by night, and brought them out and said,
not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers, in the day that I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; for they didn’t…
